composing_text: 146th Infantry Brigade; 147th Infantry Brigade; 70th Infantry Brigade
notes: Landed 13 June (Gold). 56th Brigade later replaced 70th (broken up Aug 1944).

current_activity: attacking in Operation Martlet; Tessel Wood taken
notes: Operation Martlet began 04:15 25 June with 8th Armd Bde and 250 guns; Fontenay-le-Pesnel not taken day one; Tessel Wood taken.
Took Rauray 16:00 on 27 June (70th Brigade) after fighting 12th SS; defence of Rauray from 29 June to 2 July (battle honour).

current_activity: Preliminary attacks: fights for Vendes and its neighbourhood on the XXX Corps front, taking heavy casualties
notes: Event date: 15-17 July 1944 (night of the 15th to the 17th) (Ellis, vol. I, p. 334). Event definition: In the fighting from the night of 15 July the division, in XXX Corps, fights for Vendes and its neighbourhood while the 59th Division attacks towards Noyers; positions are improved but gains are inconsiderable. Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 334: "XXX Corps was meanwhile to secure the Noyers area"; "Division fighting for Vendes and its neighbourhood". Location: Vendes, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is Vendes; the dates are those of the three-day fight. Location support: Ellis names Vendes as the place of the fight (p. 334).

current_activity: Le Havre: attacks from the north-east with the 34th Tank Brigade after the last heavy raid, to take the north plateau
notes: Event date: 10 September 1944, 17:30 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 7, 14). Event definition: I Corps begins the assault on Le Havre almost as soon as the last heavy bomber raid ends at 17:30 on 10 September; the 49th Division, with the 34th Tank Brigade under command, sets out from the north-east to capture the defences of the north plateau and then to cross the Fontaine valley to the south plateau; the 51st Division joins on its right at midnight; the division had closed round the perimeter with the 51st Division on 4 September (pp. 7 and 14). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 7: "On the 4th the two divisions closed round the perimeter"; p. 14: "Almost as soon as the last heavy bomber attack finished at 5.30 in the afternoon of the roth, an attack by I Corps began which was to continue through the night"; "The 49th Division, with the 34th Tank Brigade under command, set out from the north-east to capture the defences of the north plateau". Location: Le Havre, France (existing place PL0169) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the town of Le Havre, the objective; the attack came from the north-east and the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Le Havre as the objective (p. 14); the attack comes from the north-east. Review (British Batch 2, 28 October 2026; inferred value; old value: operation_id OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE; new value: operation_id OP-ASTONIA): the row is part of the I Corps assault on Le Havre of 10 to 12 September 1944, which Stacey, p. 331, calls a neat and expeditious three-day operation in the second week of September and names Operation Astonia; the new operation is a child of OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE, so the narrower operation replaces the broader one. The other rows under OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE are not about Le Havre.
